list.name: namespace
list.label: Instance
list.description: The instance this board reads. Empty on purpose: the chart's templates/grafana-dashboard.yaml replaces this entry with a hidden constant naming the instance it installs, so every namespace="$namespace" selector reads that instance's series and no other. There is no instance picker: each instance ships its own copy of this board, in its own Grafana folder.

list.name: instance
list.label: Instance ID
list.description: The instance ID, used to select this instance's alerts. Empty on purpose: the chart's templates/grafana-dashboard.yaml replaces this entry with a hidden constant holding the ID of the instance it installs.

title: DeviceChain — Ingest
description: Where device data enters the platform: how much is arriving, whether the MQTT backlog is keeping up, and what is being refused or lost at the door. Start with the red tiles: messages lost before being read must be zero. Each instance gets its own copy of this board, scoped to it.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Alerts firing right now for this instance that concern command delivery. An empty table means none are firing. Alerts come from the instance's Prometheus rules, so the table stays empty if those rules are not installed.

panels.title: Backlog of MQTT messages waiting to be forwarded
Messages lost before being read, over the range
panels.description: Messages the MQTT capture stream threw away before the platform read them, counted over the time range you picked. Any number above zero is real data loss: devices were told their message was received, and it was not kept. Zero is the only healthy value. If it is above zero, the forwarder fell behind the arriving traffic: check the backlog and arrival panels beside this one, add event-sources replicas, and treat the affected time window as incomplete.

panels.title: Messages lost before being read, any consumer
panels.description: The same loss count for every consumer of every platform stream, over the time range. Above zero means some stream discarded messages a consumer had not yet read. Open the Messaging board to see which stream and consumer.

panels.title: Backlog against its limit
panels.description: How full the capture backlog is, as a share of what the capture stream can hold: messages waiting to be forwarded or not yet confirmed. At 100% the stream starts discarding the oldest unread messages, and those are lost. Above 10% and rising, add event-sources replicas now; above 80% loss is close. Shows no data until MQTT traffic has been seen.

panels.title: Capture stream fill
panels.description: How full the capture stream is, by size. The stream holds both messages already forwarded and those still waiting, so a high value alone is normal. Read it together with the backlog tile, and act when the backlog is high too.

panels.title: Capture stream leader changes, over the range
panels.description: How many times the capture stream moved to a different broker server over the time range. While a move is in progress, MQTT messages that arrive are stored nowhere and no other counter sees them, so a change during active traffic can mean silent loss. Expect changes when the broker is restarted on purpose; otherwise check broker health on the Messaging board.

panels.title: Events arriving per second
panels.description: Events received from all inbound sources (MQTT, HTTP, external brokers) per second, before decoding. Compare with the backlog growth on the panel below: if arrival is steady but the backlog grows, the forwarder is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Backlog and stream fill over time
panels.description: Two lines on one scale. Backlog is the share of the capture stream's capacity holding messages not yet forwarded; at 100% the oldest unread messages are discarded. Stream fill is total size against its limit. A backlog line climbing toward 100% is the warning to act on.

targets.expr: max by (stream) ({__name__=~"devicechain_[a-z0-9]+_jetstream_stream_used_bytes", stream=~".*device-events-capture", namespace="$namespace"} / ({__name__=~"devicechain_[a-z0-9]+_jetstream_stream_limit_bytes", stream=~".*device-events-capture", namespace="$namespace"} > 0))

panels.title: Arriving vs backlog growth
panels.description: Events arriving per second, and how fast the capture backlog is growing or draining (messages per second). When the backlog line is above zero the forwarder is reading slower than events arrive, and it is the line to watch during a spike. Below zero the backlog is draining. Arrival counts every inbound source, so it is an upper bound for MQTT.

panels.title: Capture backlog in messages
panels.description: Messages waiting to be forwarded, and messages already removed from the stream that the forwarder never read. The second line should stay at zero; any value means loss has already happened or is happening.

panels.title: Events arriving by source
panels.description: Events received per second, by inbound source (the name an operator gave each transport). A source that drops to zero when it should be busy is the first thing to check after an outage.

panels.title: Refused or lost at the door
Lost: external publish failed, over the range
panels.description: Messages from an external MQTT broker that were decoded but could not be stored because publishing to the platform failed. That source does not retry, so each one is lost. Above zero: check the Messaging board for stream or broker trouble.

panels.title: Refused to protect unread data, over the range
panels.description: Messages refused because the platform is protecting messages it has not read yet (a backlog is near its limit). The sender should retry. Above zero means ingest is saturated: see the backlog tiles and add capacity.

panels.title: Held back by rate limits, over the range
panels.description: Messages shed because a tenant exceeded its ingest ceiling. This is the limit working as designed, but a tenant that is regularly limited needs a higher ceiling or a quieter fleet. See the by-priority panel below.

panels.title: Rejected as malformed, over the range
panels.description: Messages that could not be decoded, carried too many readings for one event, or had an invalid or very old timestamp. Check the device firmware or the decoder configured for the source.

panels.title: Refused: tenant deleted, over the range
panels.description: Messages refused because their tenant was deleted and its data is being removed. Expected for a short while after a deletion; devices still sending should be switched off.

panels.title: Refused: credential in MQTT body, over the range
panels.description: MQTT messages that carried a credential in the message body. The broker already authenticates the device, so the body credential is unnecessary and is refused (or stripped, while the transitional setting is on). Update the device to stop sending it.

panels.title: Refusals by reason
panels.description: Messages refused or lost per second, by reason. The healthy state is an empty chart. Publish failed and Protecting unread data mean the platform is under stress; the others point at a tenant or a device.

panels.title: Rate-limited messages by source and priority
panels.description: Messages shed at a tenant's ingest ceiling per second, by source and by priority class (the class says how important the shed traffic was; lower-priority traffic is shed first). The second line counts individual readings dropped, which can exceed messages when a message carries several.

panels.title: Decoded vs failed to decode
panels.description: Messages per second that were decoded successfully and that failed to decode, by source. A rising failed line with steady traffic usually means a device or decoder change.

panels.title: Tenant limits that could not be looked up
panels.description: Admissions metered at the platform default because the tenant's own ceiling was not known, by cause. Unreachable means user-management could not be asked and needs attention; the others settle on their own. The last line counts admissions that used the shared overflow allowance because too many unconfirmed tenant names arrived.

panels.title: Protection of the MQTT message store
Required consumers present
panels.description: 1 when every platform consumer that must exist on the broker's MQTT message store is present; 0 when one could not be created, in which case acknowledged messages of its kind are not kept. This protection is optional: with it off the tile shows no data.

panels.title: Consumers found missing, over the range
panels.description: Checks that found a required consumer missing. Each one means acknowledged MQTT messages of that kind were not kept until it was recreated. Above zero: check the broker.

panels.title: Store settings put back, over the range
panels.description: Times the platform found a setting on the broker's MQTT message store changed from what it requires and restored it. Above zero means something else is editing the store: find out what.

panels.title: Gateway streams without a size limit
panels.description: Streams of the broker's MQTT gateway that have no size limit and could not be given one. An unbounded stream can fill the broker's disk. Above zero: the platform could not set the limit, so check its broker permissions.

panels.title: Connections refused: store full, over the range
panels.description: Device connection attempts refused because the MQTT message store was above its high-water mark. The platform does this on purpose so that no more messages are accepted than it can keep. Devices reconnect later. Above zero: drain the capture backlog and check store fill.

panels.title: Connections refused: busy, over the range
panels.description: Device connection attempts refused because too many sign-in checks were already running. Devices retry. Persistent values mean the sign-in service is overloaded: add device-management replicas.

panels.title: MQTT message store fill and connection refusals
panels.description: How full the broker's MQTT message store is against its limit, and whether new device connections are being refused because of it (1 means refusing). Refusal starts at the high-water mark.

panels.title: Connection refusals per second
panels.description: Device connections refused per second, by cause: store full (deliberate protection) and busy (sign-in checks saturated). The last line counts store readings that failed, which blind the protection.

panels.title: Required consumers: waiting and unconfirmed messages
panels.description: For each platform consumer on the MQTT message store, messages not yet handed over and messages handed over but not yet confirmed. Steady growth means the consumer is stuck. Gaps in the line mean the value could not be trusted at that moment.

panels.title: Device sign-in checks by outcome
panels.description: Device credential checks per second, by kind and result. A rise in failures usually means a device fleet with a wrong or expired credential; a rise across all devices means a platform problem.

panels.title: Presence changes not recorded, over the range
panels.description: Device online or offline changes the platform saw but could not record. Each one can leave a device showing the wrong state. Above zero: check the Messaging board and the event-sources logs.

panels.title: External MQTT sources without exactly one reader
panels.description: For each external MQTT broker the platform reads, exactly one pod must be reading it. This counts sources where that is not true: zero readers means no data, two readers means duplicates. Zero is healthy. Reads zero when no external sources are configured.

panels.title: Device cache evictions, over the range
panels.description: Entries pushed out of the device sign-in cache because it was full. A high number means the cache is too small for the fleet and sign-ins go to the database more often.

panels.title: Device online and offline changes
panels.description: Device presence changes recorded per second, by new state. A burst of offline changes across many devices at once points at a network or broker event, not at the devices.

panels.title: Device sign-in cache lookups
panels.description: Lookups in the device sign-in cache per second, by result. Mostly hits is healthy. Many misses together with many evictions means the cache is too small.

panels.title: Devices registered, over the range
panels.description: Self-registration requests that succeeded over the time range: a device created, an earmarked device given its credential, or a retry recognised as one already done. A fleet being commissioned shows here; a quiet instance shows zero, which is normal.

panels.title: Refused: wrong key or secret, over the range
panels.description: Self-registration requests refused because the provision key or secret was not valid, over the time range. Every cause is counted together on purpose: an unknown tenant or key, a wrong secret, a profile that is disabled or expired. A few mean a mistyped secret; a steady stream means a fleet with the wrong secret or someone probing. The ProvisioningAuthFailuresSustained alert fires on the sustained case.

panels.title: Held back by rate limits, over the range
panels.description: Self-registration requests answered 429 over the time range, from the per-source limit or the tenant's own. Devices wait and retry, so nothing is lost, but a steady count means a limit is too tight for the fleet or every device is sharing one source address. The ProvisioningRateLimited alert fires on the sustained case.

panels.title: Refused: no free slot, over the range
panels.description: Self-registration requests answered 503 over the time range because every slot of the replica was in use. Devices retry. A steady count means registrations arrive faster than the database can take them.

panels.title: Refused: profile misconfigured, over the range
panels.description: Self-registration requests refused because the provisioning profile cannot work: its device type was deleted, its strategy is unknown, or it mints a credential type this build does not support. Above zero is an operator's to fix; the ProvisioningMisconfigured alert fires on the first.

panels.title: Registrations being worked on now
panels.description: Self-registrations the replicas are working on right now, after their request body arrived. A request still sending its body is not counted. Pinned at the slot limit means new requests are being answered 503.

panels.title: Self-registration requests by result
panels.description: Self-registration requests per second, by result. created, adopted and replayed are successes; the others are refusals. replayed is a device retrying a registration that already worked, which is healthy after a lost answer and a loop if it stays high.

panels.title: Time to answer a self-registration
panels.description: How long the median and the slowest few percent of self-registration requests take to answer, counted from the moment the handler starts, so a slow client body is included. The registration itself is one short database transaction.

panels.title: Active readers
panels.description: Replicas currently reading from the Sparkplug broker. Exactly one is healthy; zero means no data is ingested and more than one means duplicates. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data.

panels.title: Failures, over the range
panels.description: Messages that could not be ingested, broker connection failures and refused subscriptions over the time range. Above zero: check the broker address and permissions. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data.

panels.title: Sparkplug messages by type
panels.description: Messages received per second by Sparkplug message type. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data.

panels.title: Sparkplug samples skipped and failures
panels.description: Samples skipped per second by reason, and ingest failures. Skipped samples are data that was not stored. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data.

panels.title: Serving
panels.description: Replicas currently serving device registrations. Exactly one should be serving; zero means devices cannot register. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data.

panels.title: Notifications dropped, over the range
panels.description: Device notifications received but not ingested, over the time range. Above zero is data loss. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data.

panels.title: LwM2M registrations, sessions and observations
panels.description: Devices currently registered, sessions open and observations active. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data.

panels.title: LwM2M requests by response code
panels.description: Requests per second by response code, and handshake failures. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data.
